title: Local Lie brackets and the locality hypothesis
notes: On a symplectic manifold \((M,\omega)\), there are ``essentially no other Lie algebra structures'' besides the Poisson bracket, with Kirillov and others named.
statement: A meaningful precise version concerns local Lie brackets on sections of a real or complex line bundle over a smooth manifold. Such brackets are differential operators of order at most one in each entry and are described locally by Jacobi brackets, including Poisson and contact brackets. This does not classify arbitrary Lie algebra structures on the vector space \(C^\infty(M)\).
reconstruction: Locality, the line-bundle framework, and the qualification by Jacobi brackets are supplied to delimit the claim; the notes do not state a classification theorem with these hypotheses.
fate: \citet[abstract]{kirillov1976local} is a close subsequent publication by the speaker (received 25 November 1975; published 1976). Only its publisher abstract and metadata were verified here, so an exact match to the notebook's shorthand is not asserted.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Formal deformation and the reported third-cohomology condition
notes: The theorem attributed to J. Vey asserts an inequivalent formal deformation \([u,v]_t=\sum_{k\geq0}t^k B_k(u,v)\), where \(B_0\) is Poisson and \(B_k\) has order \(2k+1\) in each argument. Global definition is said to follow from \(H^3(M,\mathbb R)=0\).
statement: For a smooth symplectic manifold, seek skew bidifferential operators \(B_k\) such that the displayed series satisfies Jacobi coefficient by coefficient, with equivalence specified by invertible formal differential changes of functions. The cohomological condition in the notes is a sufficient condition reported for Vey's construction; it is not a necessary condition for existence of deformation quantization.
reconstruction: The coefficientwise interpretation and equivalence by formal differential operators make explicit what ``formal'' and ``inequivalent'' must mean. The notes's narrower phrase ``change of coordinates'' alone does not specify the customary equivalence relation.
fate: \citet[pp.~421--454]{vey1975deformation} is the named 1975 publication; its exact obstruction argument was not obtained here. The report treats it as an existing theorem, but the publication month was not verified. The later Fedosov construction gives star products on arbitrary smooth symplectic manifolds; its mechanism is checked in \citet[Sections~1--2]{emmrichweinstein1993differential}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Formal symplectic deformation quantization is established without the displayed vanishing assumption; the exact Vey formulation in this shorthand remains only partially verified.

title: The planar Moyal bracket requires mixed derivatives
notes: The coefficient \(B_k\) is drawn as the difference of the two pure \((2k+1)\)-st derivative products, divided by \((2k+1)!\), followed by dots called lower terms; on the plane or torus the lower terms are said to vanish.
statement: For a constant Poisson tensor \(P=\partial_p\otimes\partial_q-\partial_q\otimes\partial_p\), one consistent formal normalization is \[ [f,g]_t=\sum_{k\geq0}\frac{t^k}{(2k+1)!}\,\mu P^{2k+1}(f\otimes g). \] Here \(\mu\) multiplies the tensor factors. Already \(P^3\) contains the mixed terms \(-3f_{ppq}g_{qqp}+3f_{pqq}g_{qpp}\); these have the same differential order as the two displayed pure terms. The formula descends to a flat symplectic torus using periodic functions.
reconstruction: This is an explicit flat-model reconstruction. Writing \(t=h^2\), it is \((f\star_h g-g\star_h f)/(2h)\) for \(\star_h=\mu\exp(hP)\). Curvature corrections can vanish in a flat model; the binomial mixed derivatives cannot.
fate: The flat Weyl/Moyal model is described in \citet[Section~2]{emmrichweinstein1993differential}. No assertion that the notebook's two pure terms alone define a Lie bracket is retained.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The final canonical-commutator suggestion
notes: The page ends with a question mark followed by \(pq-qp=t\).
statement: This can be read as the formal Weyl-algebra relation for two generators over \(\mathbb C[[t]]\). It suggests an associative quantization whose commutator recovers a Poisson bracket after division by the parameter. The line does not specify whether existence, representations, global gluing, or comparison with the preceding deformation is being asked.
reconstruction: The Weyl-algebra interpretation is a possible identification, not a recovered definite research question. The use of the same letter \(t\) as in the previous expansion need not preserve the normalization.
fate: The relation is compatible with the local Weyl construction in \citet[Section~2]{emmrichweinstein1993differential}, but that compatibility does not identify a unique problem or its fate.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: No definite question can be recovered from this line.

title: The 1975 particle table and interaction-strength heuristic
notes: The table lists photons; electrons, muons and two massless neutrinos; protons, neutrons and pions. Approximate masses are \(0.5,105,940,140\), and gravitational, weak, electromagnetic and strong strengths are ranked by \(10^{-38},10^{-5},10^{-2},1\).
statement: The masses are approximate values in \(\mathrm{MeV}/c^2\). The table is a historical teaching selection, not an exhaustive particle classification. A dimensionless interaction strength must specify the process and energy scale; \(E_{\rm int}/m\) is not a universal constant for each interaction. Statements ordering the number of violated conservation laws by strength have no general theorem behind them. Massless neutrinos are an approximation of the then minimal model.
reconstruction: Units, scale dependence, and the distinction between a model assumption and a measured mass are supplied. No numerical modernization of this historical table is attempted.
fate: The later oscillation evidence in \citet[abstract]{fukuda1998oscillation} rules out treating all neutrinos as exactly massless. The strength ranking is retained as an introductory heuristic, not a theorem awaiting development.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The particle table is historical; the neutrino masslessness and universal strength assertions are not valid literal modern statements.

title: Spin one-half, Weyl spinors, and Lorentz boosts
notes: Rotations act by \(\exp(i\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\boldsymbol\Theta/2)\); the two boost laws are \(e_L\mapsto e^{\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\boldsymbol\psi/2}e_L\) and \(e_R\mapsto e^{-\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\boldsymbol\psi/2}e_R\), with \(v=\tanh|\boldsymbol\psi|\).
statement: The Pauli matrices generate the two-dimensional representation of \(SU(2)\). The two inequivalent Weyl representations of \(SL_2(\mathbb C)=\operatorname{Spin}^+(1,3)\) restrict to this rotation representation and have opposite boost generators. The signs depend on active/passive and left/right conventions; rapidity has \(|\mathbf v|=c\tanh|\boldsymbol\psi|\). They are representations of the spin cover, not single-valued spinor representations of \(SO^+(1,3)\).
reconstruction: The covering group and units are supplied; the notebook boost convention is retained.
fate: \citet[Section~4.1]{tong2006qft} supplies the standard spinor construction. This is exposition of pre-existing representation theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Gelfand’s covering-group explanation
notes: Gelfand draws \(SO(3)\longrightarrow SU(2)\) and explains the spinor rotation action and its extension to Lorentz transformations.
statement: The canonical surjective covering map is \(SU(2)\to SO(3)\), with kernel \(\{\pm I\}\). A rotation lifts to two elements, so an arrow in the opposite direction cannot be a globally defined inverse homomorphism. Likewise \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\to SO^+(1,3)\) is a double cover.
reconstruction: The arrow is interpreted as a covering-group explanation because of its surrounding text, not silently reversed in the diplomatic transcription.
fate: The covering description is standard; see \citet[Section~4.1]{tong2006qft}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Parity, the Weyl equations, and the Dirac mass
notes: Parity interchanges \(e_L,e_R\); the massless equations imply \(E^2=\mathbf p^2\). A bilinear \(m(e_L^\dagger e_R+e_R^\dagger e_L)\) is added and rewritten as \(\bar e(i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu-m)e\).
statement: With \(\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)\) and \(\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}\), the Dirac equation implies \((\Box+m^2)e=0\). Plane waves have \(E=\pm\sqrt{\mathbf p^2+m^2}\); the displayed positive root is the positive-energy branch. A parity-invariant charged Dirac field combines the two Weyl modules. Up to normalization, phase choices, and the stated parity and charge symmetries, its real scalar mass couples opposite chiralities.
reconstruction: The factors of \(i\), relative signs, both energy branches, and the symmetries needed for the claimed uniqueness of the mass term are supplied. Unqualified uniqueness would ignore pseudoscalar and, for neutral fields with different symmetries, Majorana masses.
fate: \citet[Sections~4.2--4.4]{tong2006qft} treats the free Dirac construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Local phase covariance introduces a connection
notes: The global phase \(e\mapsto e^{i\beta}e\) is made position dependent; the connection transforms as \(A_\mu\mapsto A_\mu-\partial_\mu\beta\), and \(\nabla_\mu=\partial_\mu+iA_\mu\). The first displayed coupling omits a gamma contraction.
statement: For \(D_\mu=\partial_\mu+iA_\mu\), \(D^{\prime}_\mu(e^{i\beta}e)=e^{i\beta}D_\mu e\). Consequently \(\bar e(i\gamma^\mu D_\mu-m)e\) is invariant under the local \(U(1)\) transformation. Its interaction is \(-\bar e\gamma^\mu A_\mu e\); a separate charge can instead be absorbed into \(A\).
reconstruction: The contraction and placement of parentheses are repaired mathematically; the malformed displayed coupling is present in the scan.
fate: \citet[Section~6.3.1]{tong2006qft} gives this standard gauge-covariant construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Curvature and the Maxwell kinetic term
notes:
To give equations for the connection, the notes add \((4e^2)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}^2\), with \(F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu\).
statement: With the preceding Lorentz signature and \(D=\partial+iA\), a standard real Minkowski Lagrangian is \[ \mathcal L=\bar e(i\gamma^\mu D_\mu-m)e-\frac{1}{4e^2}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}. \] Variation in \(A\) gives Maxwell's equations with the Dirac current. A positive quadratic sign instead belongs to the usual Euclidean action after Wick rotation.
reconstruction: Raising the tensor indices, selecting Lorentz signature consistently, and distinguishing the Euclidean sign are necessary additions; no Wick rotation appears at this point in the notes.
fate: \citet[Section~6.1]{tong2006qft} verifies the conventional Maxwell and QED action.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The scattering functional integral is formal
notes: A transition amplitude is written \(\int_{\Phi_{\rm in}}^{\Phi_{\rm out}}D\varphi\,e^{iS[\varphi]}\); \(D\varphi\) is called a natural Lebesgue measure. Free theory is Gaussian and interaction gives perturbation theory.
statement: A finite-mode or lattice regulator produces finite-dimensional oscillatory bosonic integrals and Berezin integrals for fermions, with boundary and gauge-fixing choices. Their normalized perturbative expansion defines formal Green functions and, after suitable limiting and scattering prescriptions, perturbative amplitudes. There is no nonzero locally finite translation-invariant Lebesgue measure on an infinite-dimensional topological vector space of fields.
reconstruction: The regulated/formal interpretation is supplied. It is neither a construction of an unregularized four-dimensional QED measure nor a theorem that pointwise field limits as \(t\to\pm\infty\) exist.
fate: \citet[Sections~3.1--3.3, 6.1]{tong2006qft} checks the perturbative scattering framework; it does not verify the notebook's literal measure claim.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The perturbative interpretation is established; the written infinite-dimensional Lebesgue integral is not a literal measure-theoretic definition.

title: Gelfand’s Gaussian-moment analogy and divergent cubic integral
notes: Gelfand compares the theory with \(\int e^{i(x^2+\varepsilon x^3)}dx\) and \(\int e^{-\sum a_{ij}x_ix_j+\varepsilon\sum x_i^3}dx\). The last expansion instead displays \(e^{ix^2(1+\varepsilon x^3)}\).
statement: For a positive definite real quadratic form \(Q\), every coefficient \(\int P(x)^k e^{-Q(x)}dx/k!\) exists for a polynomial \(P\); these coefficients define a formal perturbation series. If \(P=x^3\) and real \(\varepsilon\ne0\), the displayed real-line integral diverges on one tail. Oscillatory analogues require a contour or distributional prescription. The final written phase is quintic, not cubic.
reconstruction: The rigorous content retained is the coefficientwise Gaussian-moment calculation, not convergence of the formal series or the cubic exponential integral.
fate: The Wick-contraction method is standard; \citet[Section~3.3]{tong2006qft} gives the corresponding perturbative mechanism. The convergence objection follows directly from the odd leading term in the notebook's real exponent.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: A logarithmically divergent model loop integral
notes: The sample integral is \(\int_{\mathbb R^4}d^4x/((|x|^2+m_1)(|x|^2+m_2))\), without a regulator.
statement: For \(m_1,m_2>0\), the integrand is locally integrable, but its radial integral at infinity behaves like \(\int^\infty r^{-1}dr\); hence the unregularized integral diverges logarithmically. A cutoff makes it a legitimate starting point for parameterization and subtraction.
reconstruction: Positivity and the ultraviolet cutoff are supplied. The radial comparison is an elementary check of this specific notebook example, not a claim about all loop integrals.
fate: The general perturbative setting is reviewed in \citet[Section~3.2]{tong2006qft}; the explicit divergence is determined directly from the written integrand.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Feynman parameters and the missing beta normalization
notes: The identity \(1/(ab)=\int_0^1(sa+(1-s)b)^{-2}ds\) is extended to arbitrary exponents and to a simplex without gamma factors.
statement: For \(a_i>0\), \(\operatorname{Re}\lambda_i>0\), and \(\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i\), \[ \prod_i a_i^{-\lambda_i}=\frac{\Gamma(\Lambda)}{\prod_i\Gamma(\lambda_i)}\int_{s_i\geq0}\frac{\delta(1-\sum_i s_i)\prod_i s_i^{\lambda_i-1}\,ds_i}{(\sum_i s_i a_i)^\Lambda}. \] The two-denominator formula is its special case. Continuation to Lorentzian denominators additionally requires consistent branches and the pole prescription.
reconstruction: The gamma ratio and domain are restored. At \(a=b=1\), \(\lambda=\mu=2\), the notebook's right-hand side is \(1/6\), while the left-hand side is \(1\); the missing factor is \(6\).
fate: \citet[Section~5.12, equations~5.12.1 and~5.12.4]{nist2026beta} verifies the beta-integral normalization. The simplex identity follows by introducing positive Schwinger parameters and separating their sum.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Dirac Green function and the Feynman pole prescription
notes: Although the prose says ``according to Maxwell'', the equation is \((i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu-m)K=\delta\), and the Fourier inverse is \((\gamma^\mu p_\mu+m)/(p^2-m^2+i0)\).
statement: For the convention \(K_F(x)=\int d^4p\,(2\pi)^{-4}e^{-ipx}(\gamma^\mu p_\mu+m)/(p^2-m^2+i0)\), \((i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu-m)K_F=\delta\) distributionally. The usual time-ordered two-point function is \(iK_F\) in this convention. The two displaced poles encode positive-frequency propagation forward and negative-frequency propagation backward in time.
reconstruction: The Fourier sign, normalization, matrix identity on the delta function, and distinction between Green function and two-point function are supplied. ``Maxwell'' here must not be used to identify the displayed electron kernel as a photon propagator.
fate: \citet[Section~5.5]{tong2006qft} gives the free Dirac propagator.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Single-photon exchange and the diagram expansion
notes: The diagram joins two electron lines by a photon. Each emission or absorption carries \(e\), but the displayed integral is a product of four electron kernels and one photon kernel without explicit vertices or \(e^2\). More diagrams contain loops and pair creation.
statement: After a fixed gauge and propagator convention, the order-\(e^2\) electron-exchange kernel contains \[ e^2\!\int\! [S_F(x_3-z_1)\gamma^\mu S_F(z_1-x_1)]\otimes[S_F(x_4-z_2)\gamma^\nu S_F(z_2-x_2)]D_{\mu\nu}(z_1-z_2)\,d^4z_1d^4z_2, \] up to the conventional factors of \(i\), external-state contractions, and exchange antisymmetrization for identical fermions. Higher terms are organized by Wick contractions with loop signs and symmetry factors.
reconstruction: The displayed formula is reconstructed as a schematic kernel, not asserted to be a fully normalized scattering amplitude. Unclear connections in the hand-drawn third and fourth diagrams are not assigned a unique graph.
fate: \citet[Section~6.5]{tong2006qft} supplies the QED vertex and diagram rules.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Antiparticles do not make the Feynman inverse the only Green function
notes: The final lines link negative-energy levels, backward time propagation, antiparticles, and an alleged unique consistent way to bypass the poles; the terminal Russian words remain doubtful.
statement: The time-ordered vacuum propagator has the Feynman \(i0\) prescription. Retarded and advanced Green functions are also well-defined distributional inverses with different boundary conditions. Antiparticles arise in the quantized complex Dirac field; uniqueness is meaningful only after the state, ordering, and boundary conditions have been specified.
reconstruction: This separates the unambiguous pole discussion from the unreadable terminal assertion. No claim that the seminar denied antiparticles is extracted from the doubtful English phrase.
fate: \citet[Sections~5.2--5.5]{tong2006qft} gives the particle/antiparticle interpretation and the time-ordered propagator.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Charge screening and the opposite nonabelian sign
notes: The leading exchange is of order \(e^2\), the polarization correction of order \(e^4\); the notes write \(e_{\rm phys}^2<e^2\) and the reverse inequality for the strong interaction.
statement: For a cutoff description of QED, vacuum polarization screens electric charge at long distances. In a mass-independent perturbative convention with one unit-charge Dirac fermion, \(\beta(e)=e^3/(12\pi^2)+O(e^5)\). For \(SU(N_c)\) with \(N_f\) fundamental Dirac flavours, \(\beta(g)=-g^3(11N_c-2N_f)/(48\pi^2)+O(g^5)\), so the coupling decreases toward high energy when \(N_f<11N_c/2\).
reconstruction: The comparison is reconstructed as the sign of scale dependence, rather than a scheme-independent inequality between undefined bare and physical numbers. The negative beta function by itself does not prove confinement.
fate: \citet[p.~1344, equations~(8)--(9)]{grosswilczek1973ultraviolet} gives the nonabelian and fermion contributions in June 1973, before this lecture; the comparison with the Abelian sign is made on the same page.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Classification modulo compact operators
notes: For the Calkin algebra \(\mathfrak B=B(H)/K(H)\), when are \(B_1,B_2\) unitarily equivalent? The answer given is equality of essential spectra and of the indices on every component of their complement.
statement: Let \(T_1,T_2\) be bounded essentially normal operators on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. They are unitarily equivalent modulo compacts, meaning \(UT_1U^*-T_2\) is compact for a unitary \(U\) on \(H\), precisely when \(\sigma_{\rm ess}(T_1)=\sigma_{\rm ess}(T_2)=X\) and \(\operatorname{ind}(T_1-\lambda)=\operatorname{ind}(T_2-\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\notin X\). Essential normality means \([T_i,T_i^*]\) is compact. The index is constant on each complementary component.
reconstruction: Essential normality and the meaning of lifted unitary equivalence are indispensable additions. The theorem does not classify arbitrary nonnormal elements of the Calkin algebra by these data.
fate: The cited 1973 chapter, \citet[pp.~58--128]{browndouglasfillmore1973unitary}, predates the seminar; its publisher metadata was opened, not its full proof. The claim is identified as the BDF theorem with the omitted hypothesis restored, rather than as a new Atiyah theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Extensions as odd analytic K-homology
notes: The notes write \(\operatorname{Ext}(X)\cong K_1(X)\) and explain \(\operatorname{Ext}(X)\) as embeddings of \(C(X)\) in the Calkin algebra.
statement: For compact metrizable \(X\), the stable unitary-equivalence classes of extensions \(0\to K(H)\to E\to C(X)\to0\), with split extensions treated as zero, form the BDF group \(\operatorname{Ext}(C(X))\). In modern notation it is naturally the odd analytic \(K\)-homology group \(KK^1(C(X),\mathbb C)\). This is a group of extension classes, not the unquotiented set of embeddings and not generally the group \(K_1(C(X))\).
reconstruction: Metrizability, stabilization, equivalence, and the distinction between homology of the space and \(K\)-theory of its function algebra are supplied. The notation \(K_1(X)\) is retained only when explicitly understood homologically.
fate: The 1973 precursor is \citet{browndouglasfillmore1973unitary}; the full paper is \citet[pp.~265--324]{browndouglasfillmore1977extensions}. Both publisher records were checked. The modern \(KK\)-notation is a reconstruction, not claimed to occur in the seminar.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Euler’s product, partitions, and the pentagonal expansion
notes: For \(\psi(q)=\prod_{n\geq1}(1-q^n)\), the reciprocal generates partitions. The exponent in the displayed pentagonal expansion is \((n^2-3n)/2\).
statement: For \(|q|<1\), or as formal power series, \[ \psi(q)^{-1}=\sum_{n\geq0}p(n)q^n,\quad p(0)=1,\qquad \psi(q)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^kq^{k(3k-1)/2}. \] Each coefficient is finite in the formal interpretation.
reconstruction: The correct pentagonal exponent and the bilateral index set are supplied. The notebook exponent would even give negative powers at small positive indices.
fate: These classical formulas are recorded in \citet[Section~27.14(ii), equations~27.14.3--5]{nist2026dlmf}; no 1975 novelty is suggested.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Jacobi’s cubic Euler-product identity
notes: The cube is \(\psi(q)^3=\sum_{n\geq0}(-1)^n(2n+1)q^{n(n+1)/2}\), with Jacobi named.
statement: The displayed identity holds for \(|q|<1\) and coefficientwise in \(\mathbb Z[[q]]\). It is the rank-one member of the eta-product/root-system family, after the appropriate leading power of \(q\) is separated.
reconstruction: Only the convergence/formal interpretation and the distinction between \(\eta\) and \(\psi\) are supplied.
fate: \citet[Section~2, pp.~636--638]{dyson1972missed} explicitly identifies Jacobi's power \(3\) in the established sequence. This revisits the eta-power discussion in 1971-269.3.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The discriminant and the exponent 24
notes: The notation is \(\eta(q)=q^{1/24}\psi(q)\), with \(\eta(q)^{24}=\sum\tau(n)q^n\); a similar formula for power \(10\) is mentioned.
statement: For \(z\) in the upper half-plane and \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(\eta(z)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\geq1}(1-q^n)\) and \(\Delta(z)=\eta(z)^{24}=\sum_{n\geq1}\tau(n)q^n\). Thus \(\tau(1)=1\). Powers \(10\) and \(24\) have explicit lattice-sum identities, but the notes state no particular power-\(10\) summation.
reconstruction: The variable \(z\), branch convention \(q^{1/24}=e^{2\pi iz/24}\), and lower index \(1\) are explicit here. The phrase about power \(10\) is catalogued without inventing its omitted formula.
fate: \citet[equations~(1)--(3), pp.~636--637]{dyson1972missed} gives the discriminant and explains Winquist's power \(10\). Earlier occurrences are 1971-269.1--3.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Macdonald identities in Kostant’s character form
notes: The power is \(\dim K\), and the sum has terms \(\chi_\lambda(a)\dim V_\lambda\) with \(\chi_\lambda(a)\in\{0,\pm1\}\); the exponent is left unspecified.
statement: For a compact connected simply connected simple Lie group \(K\), let \(\rho\) be half the sum of positive roots and use the Killing-form normalization to identify weights with the Cartan subalgebra. For Kostant's principal element \(a=\exp(2\pi i\,2\rho)\), \[ \prod_{n\geq1}(1-q^n)^{\dim K}=\sum_{\lambda\in P_+}\chi_\lambda(a)\dim V_\lambda\,q^{(\lambda+\rho,\lambda+\rho)-(\rho,\rho)},\qquad \chi_\lambda(a)\in\{0,1,-1\}. \] The inner product here is the one in the cited theorem; arbitrary root-length normalization changes the exponents.
reconstruction: Simplicity, simple connectedness, the principal element, and the Casimir exponent replace the omitted hypotheses and dots. ``Dimensions of compact groups'' alone is too broad a description of the precise theorem.
fate: Macdonald's underlying identities appeared in 1972 \citep{macdonald1972affine}. \citet[Theorems~0.1 and~2.1]{kostant2003euler} restates the character formula and explicitly identifies its original 1976 Theorem~3.1. This supports class A for Kostant's particular formulation, not a new priority claim for the older product identities.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The spectral-zeta fragment
notes: After the character identity, the page records ``Kostant: \(\operatorname{Sp}(-\Delta+a)^{-s}\), etc.''
statement: A spectral zeta function of a positive elliptic operator can be defined for sufficiently large \(\operatorname{Re}s\), and a group element can enter an equivariant trace. However, the notes do not specify the operator domain, the meaning of \(a\), whether it is added or acts by translation, or any asserted identity.
reconstruction: An equivariant heat/zeta-trace connection is a possible interpretation only. The group element \(a\) from the preceding line cannot simply be treated as a scalar spectral shift without additional information.
fate: The heat-kernel connection in \citet[Introduction]{kostant2003euler} provides thematic context, but does not verify this literal expression.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The intended spectral formula is not identifiable with sufficient precision.

title: Gelfand’s complex-exponent suggestion
notes: Gelfand writes \(\psi(q)^z\), followed by a question mark, with \(z\in\mathbb C\).
statement:
There is a canonical analytic definition on \(|q|<1\):
     \[\psi(q)^z=\exp\!\left(z\sum_{n\geq1}\log(1-q^n)\right),\]
     using the branch equal to \(1\) at \(q=0\). Its formal coefficients are polynomials in \(z\). This observation does not determine whether Gelfand wanted analytic continuation, coefficient formulas, representation-theoretic interpolation, or another property.
reconstruction: The elementary definition is supplied only to show that existence of a complex power is not itself a uniquely recoverable open problem. It is not equated with the earlier definite question about exponent \(26\), GP-1971-41.
fate: \citet[Introduction]{kostant2003euler} studies coefficients of general powers, but the notebook specifies no assertion that can be matched to one of its theorems.

title: The enlarged symmetry of massless lepton kinetic terms
notes: The kinetic terms for \(e_L,\nu_L,e_R\) have \(SU_L(2)\times U_R(1)\times U_L(1)\) symmetry; another lepton family is indicated. A preceding line still includes the electron mass term.
statement: For a massless left Weyl doublet \(L=(\nu_L,e_L)^T\) and a right Weyl singlet \(e_R\), the free kinetic Lagrangian is invariant under \(U(2)_L\times U(1)_R\). At the Lie-algebra level this is \(\mathfrak{su}(2)_L\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_L\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_R\); the product-group notation suppresses a finite central quotient. A nonzero bare Dirac mass selecting the electron component breaks the independent left-doublet symmetry.
reconstruction: The massless restriction and global central quotient are supplied. The doublet order is changed explicitly to the usual convention for later charge assignments.
fate: \citet[p.~1264, equations~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons} starts from these kinetic symmetries and selects the gauged combination. It was published 20 November 1967.

u}=\partial_\mu W_

title: Neutral mixing requires a hypercharge assignment
notes: A right-handed \(U(1)\) field \(B\) and \(A_\gamma=A^3\cos\theta+B\sin\theta\) are written, without a complete left-handed \(B\)-coupling or symmetry-breaking sector.

title: Four flavours and three colours in the quark count
notes: The last line counts twelve quarks as four flavours times three colours.
statement: In the four-flavour model under discussion, the internal one-particle labels are \(\{u,d,s,c\}\times\{1,2,3\}\), giving twelve flavour--colour labels. This does not mean twelve flavours, and it does not count spin or antiquark labels.

title: Differential polynomials and total differentiation
notes: The algebra consists of polynomials in \(u,u',u'',\ldots\), and differentiation is \(D=\sum u^{(k+1)}\partial/\partial u^{(k)}\).
statement: Let \(\mathcal A=\mathbb R[u_0,u_1,\ldots]\), each element depending on finitely many variables, and \(D=\sum_{j\geq0}u_{j+1}\partial_{u_j}\). Evaluation at a smooth function, \(u_j=\partial_x^j u(x)\), intertwines \(D\) with \(\partial_x\). Each formal sum acts finitely on every element of \(\mathcal A\).
reconstruction: Finite dependence and the evaluation interpretation are explicit additions. The variables are algebraically independent before evaluation.
fate: The framework is developed in \citet[Sections~8--10]{gelfanddikii1976fractional}, received 22 June 1976 and published in 1976. The source's differential-polynomial construction was read.

title: The evolutionary Lie bracket
notes:
For two differential polynomials the notes write
     \[[P,Q]=\sum_{k\geq0}\left(D^kP\,\frac{\partial Q}{\partial u_k}-D^kQ\,\frac{\partial P}{\partial u_k}\right).\]
statement: For \(P\in\mathcal A\), define the evolutionary derivation \(\mathcal D_P=\sum_{k\geq0}D^k(P)\partial_{u_k}\). Then \([P,Q]=\mathcal D_P(Q)-\mathcal D_Q(P)\) is a Lie bracket, and \([\mathcal D_P,\mathcal D_Q]=\mathcal D_{[P,Q]}\). The injection \(P\mapsto\mathcal D_P\) follows from \(\mathcal D_P(u_0)=P\); Jacobi follows from the derivation commutator.
reconstruction: \ours\ The short derivation argument makes the Jacobi claim precise and fixes the sign convention, without introducing a Poisson bracket on the original jet variables.
fate: \citet[Section~10, equation~(24)]{gelfanddikii1976fractional} gives the same evolutionary bracket in the subsequent joint paper.

title: Povzner’s identification with compatible evolution equations
notes: Povzner associates \(a\) with \(u_t=a\), explains its derivation on all derivatives of \(u\), and identifies the bracket of these derivations.
statement: For autonomous differential-polynomial flows \(u_t=P[u]\) and \(u_s=Q[u]\), compatibility of the formal prolonged vector fields is \([P,Q]=0\). Indeed \(\partial_tQ[u]-\partial_sP[u]=\mathcal D_PQ-\mathcal D_QP\). This is a formal jet-space statement; it alone does not establish existence, uniqueness, or commuting solution maps for a chosen PDE function space.

title: Tau as the coefficients of the discriminant
notes: Manin opens with \(x\prod_{n\geq1}(1-x^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\geq1}\tau(n)x^n\).
statement: The identity defines integers \(\tau(n)\), \(n\geq1\), as the coefficients of \(\Delta(q)=q\prod_{m\geq1}(1-q^m)^{24}\), with \(\tau(1)=1\). It is valid formally and analytically for \(|q|<1\).
reconstruction: Only the formal/analytic interpretation is supplied. This occurrence repeats 1975-366.3 and 1971-269.1, rather than introducing a second tau function.
fate: \citet[equation~(1), p.~636]{dyson1972missed} gives the same definition before the seminar.

title: The unexplained nonalgorithmic qualification
notes: The heading calls the expressions ``not obtained by a finite algorithm'', while the list itself begins with a finite coefficient-extraction procedure.
statement: For any given positive integer \(n\), \(\tau(n)\) is computable by truncating \(q\prod_{m=1}^{n-1}(1-q^m)^{24}\) modulo \(q^{n+1}\). Therefore a literal assertion that no finite algorithm computes \(\tau(n)\) is false. The phrase may instead concern deriving one description from another or the conceptual diversity of the formulas; no complexity model or quantified claim is stated.
reconstruction: The finite coefficient algorithm is an elementary consequence of the supplied definition. The possible alternative reading is explicitly conjectural and is not indexed as a research problem.
fate: No exact noncomputability or complexity assertion was identified. The surrounding explicit coefficient formulas in \citet[Section~1.3]{manin1973periods} reinforce the need to retain this textual uncertainty.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The qualification is not a recoverable mathematical conjecture.

title: The combinatorial expansion needs multiplicities
notes: The first expression sums \((-1)^k\) over ordered-by-size partitions of \(n-1\), with at most 24 consecutive equality signs. No colours or binomial coefficients are shown.
statement: The literal product expansion is \[ \tau(n)=\sum_{\substack{0\leq r_j\leq24\ (j\geq1)\\\sum j r_j=n-1}}(-1)^{\sum r_j}\prod_j\binom{24}{r_j}. \] Only \(j\leq n-1\) contribute. Equivalently, each selected part size comes with a subset of 24 labelled copies; it can occur at most 24 times, hence at most 23 equality signs within a run.
reconstruction: The binomial multiplicities are mandatory. At \(n=2\), an unweighted partition count gives \(-1\), while the product gives \(-24\). This counterexample is independent of the ambiguity between copies and equality signs.
fate: The reconstruction follows directly by the binomial theorem from the discriminant product in \citet[equation~(1)]{dyson1972missed}. The accompanying exact-arithmetic code independently computes the coefficients through \(n=50\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Dyson’s five-variable formula
notes: The second expression is \(\tau(n)=(1!2!3!4!)^{-1}\sum\prod_{i<j}(u_i-u_j)\), subject to \(\sum u_i=0\), \(\sum u_i^2=10n\), and \(u_i\equiv i\pmod5\).
statement: For every positive integer \(n\), sum over all labelled integer 5-tuples satisfying those three conditions. Then the displayed Vandermonde sum equals \(\tau(n)\); its finiteness follows from the sum-of-squares condition. The congruences are attached to the labels, so no extra quotient by permutations is taken.
reconstruction: The labelled summation convention and positivity of \(n\) are made explicit; no further mathematical repair is required.
fate: \citet[equation~(2), pp.~636--637]{dyson1972missed} prints exactly this formula. His Gibbs lecture was delivered 17 January 1972 and the paper appeared in September 1972; this repeats 1971-269.2.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Ramanujan’s divisor-convolution identity
notes: The third formula is \(\tau(n)=\frac{65}{756}\sigma_{11}(n)+\frac{691}{756}\sigma_5(n)-\frac{691}{3}\sum_{m=1}^{n-1}\sigma_5(m)\sigma_5(n-m)\).
statement: For \(\sigma_k(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}d^k\) and \(n\geq1\), this identity is correct. It follows by comparing coefficients in \(E_6^2=E_{12}-(762048/691)\Delta\), using \(E_6=1-504\sum\sigma_5(n)q^n\) and \(E_{12}=1+(65520/691)\sum\sigma_{11}(n)q^n\).
reconstruction: The modular-form identity explains the otherwise opaque constants. The coefficient comparison is a reconstruction, not a second formula written in the notes.
fate: The modular-form basis theorem is checked in \citet[Proposition~4.16]{milne2017modular}; the weight-12 normalization is checked independently in \citet[Section~3]{brouwerleech}. Direct Euler-product coefficients and a separate divisor recurrence agree with the notebook convolution for \(1\leq n\leq50\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The congruence modulo 691
notes: The convolution formula is followed by \(\tau(n)\equiv\sigma_{11}(n)\pmod{691}\), attributed to Ramanujan.
statement: For every positive integer \(n\), \(\tau(n)-\sigma_{11}(n)\) is divisible by \(691\). Indeed multiply the preceding identity by \(756\), reduce modulo \(691\), and use \(756\equiv65\pmod{691}\) with \(65\) invertible modulo \(691\).
reconstruction: The elementary modular reduction is supplied; it does not require the later Galois-representation construction.
fate: \citet[Section~1.3, p.~374]{manin1973periods} explicitly recovers this already classical congruence from his coefficient theorem. It also occurs in 1973-305.9.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The assertion that there are only two rank-24 forms
notes: Integral quadratic forms of determinant one in 24 variables are said to number ``2 in all''; neither evenness nor positive definiteness is written.
statement: Even after imposing positive definiteness and even unimodularity on the associated lattice, there are more than two classes. For example \(E_8^{\oplus3}\), \(D_{24}^+\), and the Leech lattice are distinguished by their numbers of norm-two vectors: \(720\), \(1104\), and \(0\). Here \(D_{24}=\{x\in\mathbb Z^{24}:\sum x_i\text{ is even}\}\) and \(D_{24}^+=D_{24}\cup((1/2,\ldots,1/2)+D_{24})\); the index-two extension is even and unimodular, and its new coset has minimal squared norm \(6\).
reconstruction: This explicit three-lattice counterexample suffices; a full classification is not needed for the correction. The nearby number two may refer to the dimension of the weight-12 modular-form space, but that is an interpretation, not a legible correction of the scan.
fate: \citet[Theorems~1.1--1.3 and Section~3]{brouwerleech} checks the Leech and theta-series facts and distinguishes the two rank-16 lattices from the two-dimensional weight-12 space. The \(D_{24}^+\) count above is the elementary root count \(2\cdot24\cdot23\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Recovering tau from a rank-24 lattice theta series
notes: The fourth formula expresses \(\tau(n)\) as a linear combination of the number of representations \(Q_{24}=n\) and \(\sigma_{11}(n)\), with constants obtained from small coefficients.
statement: Let \(L\) be an even positive definite unimodular lattice of rank 24, set \(Q(v)=(v,v)/2\), and \(r_L(n)=\#\{v\in L:Q(v)=n\}\). Then \[ r_L(n)=\frac{65520}{691}\sigma_{11}(n)+c_L\tau(n),\qquad c_L=r_L(1)-\frac{65520}{691}. \] Thus \(\tau(n)\) is recovered by division by \(c_L\ne0\); nonvanishing follows because \(r_L(1)\) is an integer. This uses \(\Theta_L\in M_{12}(SL_2(\mathbb Z))=\mathbb C E_{12}\oplus\mathbb C\Delta\).
reconstruction: The lattice hypotheses and half-norm convention are necessary. Determinant one alone is insufficient for this weight and full modular group. The constant coefficient and the coefficient of \(q\) already determine the two constants.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.2 and Section~3]{brouwerleech} verifies the theta-series argument and the explicit Leech instance. This is established modular-form theory, not a new classification of forms.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Manin’s finite coefficient formula and its boundary weights
notes: The fifth expression sums over \(n=\Delta\Delta'+\delta\delta'\), but its polynomial is printed as \((\Delta^8\delta^2-\Delta^2\delta^8)+(691/6)(\Delta^6\delta^4-\Delta^4\delta^6)\), subtracted from \(\sigma_{11}(n)\).
statement: The corrected factorized form is \[ \tau(n)=\sigma_{11}(n)-\frac{691}{18}\sum{}'\Delta^2\delta^2(\Delta^2-\delta^2)^3. \] Sum over integers \(\Delta>\delta>0\) satisfying either \(\Delta'>\delta'>0\), \(n=\Delta\Delta'+\delta\delta'\), or \(\delta'=0\), \(\Delta\mid n\), \(\Delta'=n/\Delta\), and \(0<\delta/\Delta\leq1/2\). In the latter case the boundary \(\delta/\Delta=1/2\) has weight \(1/2\). Expanding the polynomial gives coefficient \(691/18\) on the first difference and \(-691/6\) on the second.
reconstruction: Both coefficients and the boundary weight are restored. At \(n=2\), the corrected sum gives \(-24\); even granting the missing half weight, the notebook polynomial gives \(-841\). The factorized formula was independently checked for \(n\leq50\) against two exact coefficient algorithms; this finite check is not offered as a proof for all \(n\).
fate: \citet[Section~1.3, pp.~373--374; proof in Section~5]{manin1973periods} is the direct earlier publication. The summation region and half-weight rule were read; the poor formula OCR was cross-checked by the factorization and exact computation. Russian publication was 1973, whereas the opened English translation carries copyright 1975; neither is inferred merely from receipt dates.

title: Recursive computation using partition numbers
notes: The sixth expression uses \(P(q)=\sum p(n)q^n=\prod(1-q^n)^{-1}\), but writes the inner sum from \(n=1\) in \(\Delta=qP^{-24}\). It proposes recovering \(\tau\) recursively from \(p\).
statement: The invertible formal series is \(P(q)=\sum_{n\geq0}p(n)q^n\), with \(p(0)=1\). Thus \(\Delta(q)=qP(q)^{-24}\) and ordinary series inversion gives a finite recursion for each coefficient. An independent recurrence from logarithmic differentiation is \((n-1)\tau(n)=-24\sum_{m=1}^{n-1}\sigma_1(m)\tau(n-m)\), \(n\geq2\).
reconstruction: The lower index is repaired. The divisor recurrence is explicitly an additional elementary verification device, not asserted to be the recursion Manin wrote.
fate: \citet[equations~27.14.3 and~27.14.7]{nist2026dlmf} verifies the partition normalization. The product and derivative recurrences independently agree through \(n=50\) in the supplied computation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The convergent Rademacher series and its phases
notes: A Hardy--Ramanujan--Rademacher series is written with a phase depending on \(1/k\) rather than \(h/k\), an asserted \(\omega_{h,k}^{24}=1\), and a derivative of a normalized hyperbolic sine. The exponential-only predecessor is contrasted with it.
statement: For \(n\geq1\), put \(t=n-1/24\), \(C=\pi\sqrt{2/3}\), and \[ A_k(n)=\sum_{\substack{h\bmod k\\(h,k)=1}}e^{\pi i s(h,k)-2\pi inh/k},\quad s(h,k)=\sum_{r=1}^{k-1}\frac r k\left(\frac{hr}{k}-\left\lfloor\frac{hr}{k}\right\rfloor-\frac12\right). \] Then \[ p(n)=\frac1{\pi\sqrt2}\sum_{k\geq1}\sqrt{k}\,A_k(n)\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{\sinh(C\sqrt t/k)}{\sqrt t}\right|_{t=n-1/24}. \] The series converges. The factor \(e^{\pi i s(h,k)}\) does not in general have order dividing 24.
reconstruction: This complete conventional normalization replaces the malformed formula. For instance \(s(1,5)=1/5\), so \((e^{\pi i/5})^{24}\ne1\). The Hardy--Ramanujan truncation is an asymptotic method, not the same convergent series with \(\sinh\) simply replaced by \(e^x\).
fate: \citet[Section~27.14(iii), equations~27.14.8--11]{nist2026dlmf} gives the convergent series, phases, and historical distinction between the 1918 asymptotic and Rademacher's 1938 treatment.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Hecke multiplicativity of tau
notes: The seventh entry underlines \(\tau(mn)=\tau(m)\tau(n)\) when \((m,n)=1\), noting that this is not apparent from the earlier formulas.
statement: The normalized cusp form \(\Delta\), spanning the one-dimensional space \(S_{12}(SL_2(\mathbb Z))\), is a simultaneous Hecke eigenform. With the conventional normalized Hecke operators, \(T_n\Delta=\tau(n)\Delta\), and \(T_mT_n=T_{mn}\) for coprime \(m,n\), giving the displayed multiplicativity.
reconstruction: The Hecke interpretation and normalization are supplied as the explanation. No assertion of multiplicativity for noncoprime arguments is made.
fate: \citet[Proposition~5.18 and Corollary~5.20]{milne2017modular} verifies the standard argument. Earlier relevant occurrences are 1973-304.8--9.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Prime-power coefficients are complete symmetric sums
notes: After \(\tau(p)=\theta_p+\bar\theta_p\) and \(\theta_p\bar\theta_p=p^{11}\), the notes underline \(\tau(p^a)=\theta_p^a+\bar\theta_p^a\).
statement: If \(\alpha_p,\beta_p\) are the roots of \(T^2-\tau(p)T+p^{11}\), then \[ \sum_{a\geq0}\tau(p^a)T^a=\frac1{(1-\alpha_pT)(1-\beta_pT)},\qquad \tau(p^a)=\sum_{j=0}^a\alpha_p^{a-j}\beta_p^j. \] Equivalently \(\tau(p^{a+1})=\tau(p)\tau(p^a)-p^{11}\tau(p^{a-1})\). A sum of just the two powers describes a trace of a Frobenius power, not this Hecke coefficient.
reconstruction: The distinction is decisive already at \(p=2,a=2\): the notebook expression is \(-3520\), while \(\tau(4)=-1472\). The complete sum, or its quotient \((\alpha^{a+1}-\beta^{a+1})/(\alpha-\beta)\) when distinct, repairs the formula.
fate: \citet[Corollary~5.20]{milne2017modular} verifies the recurrence. The small counterexample is checked independently by direct product multiplication and the divisor recurrence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The two-dimensional l-adic representation
notes: The eighth entry says that \(\tau\) is the trace of a representation and names Serre, Deligne, Grothendieck, Weil, Kuga, and Sato. The target is drawn as \(\mathbb Q_\ell^2\).
statement: For every prime \(\ell\), the eigenform \(\Delta\) has a continuous two-dimensional \(\ell\)-adic representation \(\rho_\ell:G_{\mathbb Q}\to GL_2(\mathbb Q_\ell)\), unramified outside \(\ell\), with \(\det(1-\rho_\ell(\operatorname{Frob}_p)T)=1-\tau(p)T+p^{11}T^2\) for \(p\ne\ell\), choosing Frobenius and dual conventions to give determinant \(p^{11}\). In particular \(\tau(p)\) is a trace at primes; the preceding item explains why \(\tau(p^a)\) is not usually the trace of the \(a\)-th power.
reconstruction: The group-valued target, continuity, ramification restriction, and convention are supplied. A vector space is the representation space, not the target group of the homomorphism.
fate: \citet[Sections~3--4, especially Theorem~4.9]{deligne1971modulaires} constructs the cohomological representation. The Bourbaki talk was given in February 1969; the collected publication is 1971, so this is established before the seminar.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Deligne’s bound does not make the roots purely imaginary
notes: The text calls \(\theta_p\) ``purely imaginary (nonreal)'', and attributes the result to Deligne's proof of the Weil conjectures.
statement: The roots of \(T^2-\tau(p)T+p^{11}\) have complex absolute value \(p^{11/2}\), and \(|\tau(p)|\leq2p^{11/2}\). Since \(\tau(p)\) is an integer and \(2p^{11/2}\) is irrational, equality cannot occur; the roots are a nonreal conjugate pair. They need not be purely imaginary: at \(p=2\), their real part is \(\tau(2)/2=-12\).
reconstruction: The distinction between \ru{чисто мнимые} and \ru{невещественные} is mathematical, not an English mistranslation. The strictness and small-prime counterexample are elementary consequences of the established bound.
fate: \citet[Theorem~5.6]{deligne1971modulaires} gives the implication Weil \(\Rightarrow\) Ramanujan; \citet[Theorem~1.6]{deligne1974weil} proves the needed weight statement. The latter was publicly published in 1974, not merely received then; it precedes this talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Eta transformations and the invariant sixth differential
notes: Eta is rewritten in the upper-half-plane variable, with an extraneous \(n\) in the leading exponential. Translation and inversion laws are given, and \(\eta^{24}(z)(dz)^6\) is called invariant.
statement: For \(\operatorname{Im}z>0\), \(\eta(z)=e^{2\pi iz/24}\prod_{n\geq1}(1-e^{2\pi inz})\), \(\eta(z+1)=e^{\pi i/12}\eta(z)\), and \(\eta(-1/z)=\sqrt{-iz}\,\eta(z)\), with the holomorphic square root positive at \(z=i\). Therefore \(\Delta(\gamma z)=(cz+d)^{12}\Delta(z)\) for \(\gamma\in SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), and \(\Delta(z)(dz)^6\) is invariant under pullback.
reconstruction: The leading exponent, square-root branch, and group are specified. The multiplier of eta has finite order in the transformation law; this does not justify the different \(\omega_{h,k}^{24}=1\) assertion in the partition formula.
fate: \citet[equations~27.14.12--14]{nist2026dlmf} verifies the eta definition and multiplier formula. This is classical exposition.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The graded ring generated by E4 and E6
notes: The notes assert that the ring of modular forms is \(\mathbb C[E_4,E_6]\) and identify the nonconstant coefficients with \(\sigma_3(n)\) and \(\sigma_5(n)\), without their normalization factors.
statement: For holomorphic scalar modular forms on \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), holomorphic also at the cusp, \[ M_* = \bigoplus_{k\geq0}M_k(SL_2(\mathbb Z))=\mathbb C[E_4,E_6], \] where \(E_4=1+240\sum_{n\geq1}\sigma_3(n)q^n\), \(E_6=1-504\sum_{n\geq1}\sigma_5(n)q^n\), and \(\Delta=(E_4^3-E_6^2)/1728\). Homogeneous polynomial identities therefore yield coefficient convolutions such as 1975-370.4.
reconstruction: The group, cusp condition, grading, constant coefficients, and scaling factors are essential. The theorem is not a statement about all levels, meromorphic forms, or arbitrary multiplier systems.
fate: \citet[Proposition~4.16 and p.~78]{milne2017modular} proves the structure and supplies the two normalized generators, using half the conventional weight in its subscripts. Earlier occurrences are 1973-304.6--7.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Rademacher contours and cusp singularities
notes: The explanation of formula six draws circles tangent at rational points and successive integration contours; it calls the boundary singularities poles of infinite order.
statement: Coefficient extraction for \(P(q)=\prod(1-q^n)^{-1}\), followed by \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), deforms a contour through arcs associated with rational cusps (Ford circles in the standard construction). Modular transformations give local expansions contributing the sums \(A_k(n)\). The analytic boundary singularities at roots of unity are not meromorphic poles of a finite order; ``pole of infinite order'' is informal terminology.
reconstruction: The identification of the circles as Ford circles and the modular coefficient-extraction mechanism are reconstructed from the labelled Rademacher diagram. No error estimate for a particular drawn truncation is inferred.
fate: The resulting convergent coefficient formula is checked in \citet[equations~27.14.9--11]{nist2026dlmf}; this verifies the endpoint, while the exact hand-drawn contour parametrization remains schematic.

title: Kostant’s identity revisited with a missing power
notes: The final formula again sums \(\chi_\lambda(a)\dim V_\lambda q^{c(\lambda)}\), now with \(c(\lambda)=(\lambda+\rho,\lambda+\rho)-(\rho,\rho)\), but the left side is only \(\psi(q)\).
statement: With the compact simple simply connected group and Killing normalization of 1975-366.4, the left side is \(\psi(q)^{\dim K}\), and the displayed Casimir exponent is correct in that normalization. The root-system character values are again \(0,\pm1\).
reconstruction: The omitted dimension power is restored by direct comparison with P000610 and with the verified theorem; the new occurrence is kept because the exponent is supplied here for the first time in these notes.

title: Heisenberg operators and their symplectic normalizer
notes: The operators \(a(x,\nu^{-1}\partial_x)\), linear in position and momentum, are normalized by automorphisms of \(S'(\mathbb R^\ell)\). The quotient by nonzero scalar operators is identified with \(\operatorname{Sp}(\ell)\).
statement: Let \(Q_jf=x_jf\), \(P_jf=-i\hbar\partial_jf\), with \(\hbar>0\), on \(\mathcal S(\mathbb R^\ell)\subset L^2(\mathbb R^\ell)\subset\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^\ell)\). Their commutators encode the real symplectic form on \(\mathbb R^{2\ell}\). An invertible continuous complex-linear implementer preserving the common Schwartz domain and the real linear span of the \(Q_j,P_j\) induces a real symplectic transformation. In the irreducible Schrödinger representation, implementers of a fixed transformation differ by a scalar; allowing all nonzero scalar multiples gives kernel \(\mathbb C^\times\), while unitary implementers have kernel \(U(1)\).
reconstruction: The real structure, continuity, irreducible Schrödinger representation, and common invariant Schwartz domain are supplied. These conditions delimit the phrase \emph{automorphisms of distributions}; arbitrary algebraic automorphisms of \(S'\) are not being classified.

title: Quadratic generating functions and unitary Fourier kernels
notes: For a real quadratic \(A(x,x')\), the notes write a kernel proportional to \(\Delta(A)e^{\nu A(x,x')}\), with \(\Delta(A)=\sqrt{\det A''}\), and the canonical relation \(p=A_x,\ p'=-A_{x'}\).
statement:
Assume \(A(x,y)\) is a real homogeneous quadratic form and its mixed Hessian \(B=\partial_x\partial_y A\) is invertible. The equations \(p=\partial_xA,\ p'=-\partial_yA\) define a linear symplectic map. For any phase \(\zeta\in U(1)\),
     \[ (T_Af)(x)=\zeta(2\pi\hbar)^{-\ell/2}|\det B|^{1/2}\int_{\mathbb R^\ell}e^{iA(x,y)/\hbar}f(y)\,dy \]
     defines a unitary operator on \(L^2\), initially on Schwartz functions and then by extension. It factors into quadratic phase multipliers, an invertible linear substitution with its Jacobian factor, and a Fourier transform.
reconstruction: Here \(\nu=i/\hbar\); the determinant means the mixed Hessian, and its absolute value supplies the modulus. The complex square-root phase in the notebook must be chosen consistently. Symplectic maps for which this mixed-coordinate generating function fails require other charts or products of such operators.
fate: The explicit kernels and elementary factorization appear in \citet[Section~1, equations~(1.1)--(1.5)]{degosson1990maslov}. The formula verifies the local chart construction, with its missing determinant and phase qualifications.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: Unitarity alone does not select the metaplectic double cover
notes: The line \ru{Унитарность} \(\Rightarrow\) \ru{метапл. группа} is followed by \(|c|=1\), then by the instruction to take \(c=\pm1\).
statement:
All unitary canonical implementers form a central \(U(1)\)-extension of \(\operatorname{Sp}(2\ell,\mathbb R)\). The metaplectic group is a distinguished subgroup defined by coherent phase choices and fits into
     \[1\longrightarrow\{\pm I\}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mp}(2\ell,\mathbb R)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}(2\ell,\mathbb R)\longrightarrow1.\]
     Multiplying a unitary implementer by an arbitrary phase preserves unitarity and its underlying symplectic map. Thus the displayed implication requires the additional normalization.
reconstruction: The modern notation \(\operatorname{Sp}(2\ell,\mathbb R)\) denotes the group written \(\operatorname{Sp}(\ell)\) in the notes. The double cover is the corrected conclusion after phase normalization, not a consequence of \(|c|=1\) alone.
fate: \citet[Section~1, Theorem~1]{degosson1990maslov} states the double-cover construction, using discrete phase indices in the generators. Earlier seminar occurrences are 1973-312.1--2.

title: Composition phases and the Maslov sign
notes: The notebook writes \(S_AS_{A'}=S_{A''}\) and, when \(s_As_{A'}s_{A''}=e\), the doubly underlined identity \(S_AS_{A'}S_{A''}=\pm E\), with its sign linked to the Maslov index.

In a nondegenerate quadratic-kernel chart, Gaussian integration contributes the signature phase \(e^{i\pi\operatorname{sgn}(H)/4}\), where \(H\) is the Hessian in the integrated intermediate variables. The discrete phase indices must incorporate this contribution. For arbitrary unitary lifts, the corresponding product can instead be any scalar in \(U(1)\).
reconstruction: The triple-product assertion is separated from a globally defined multiplication law for generating functions: compositions may leave a given chart, and an unqualified assignment \(A\mapsto S_A\) does not provide a global section of the cover.

title: Liouville integrability and quadratures
notes: Perelomov defines complete integrability by \(n\) first integrals in involution for \(H=\frac12\sum p_k^2+U(q)\); Gelfand recalls Liouville's theorem that the system can then be solved by quadratures.
statement: On a smooth \(2n\)-dimensional symplectic manifold, suppose \(F_1=H,F_2,\ldots,F_n\) Poisson commute and \(dF_1,\ldots,dF_n\) are independent on the regular region under consideration. The local integration procedure reduces the motion to quadratures. A compact connected regular common level is an \(n\)-torus, with action--angle coordinates in a neighborhood and linear motion on each torus. Without compactness this global torus conclusion does not follow.

title: The pendulum quadrature is not a second independent integral
notes: For \(H=\frac12p^2+\sin q\), the next line reads \ru{2-й инт. --- эллиптич. ф-я}, rendered as a second integral and an elliptic function.
statement:
On an energy level \(H=E\), \(\dot q=p\) gives
     \[t-t_0=\pm\int_{q_0}^{q}\frac{ds}{\sqrt{2(E-\sin s)}}.\]
     Away from turning points this is a local quadrature; its inversion is expressed through elliptic functions for generic energy. The critical energies \(E=\pm1\) require separate limiting or equilibrium solutions. There cannot be a second functionally independent first integral on a regular two-dimensional phase region.
reconstruction: The abbreviation is interpreted as the second integration step, not an additional independent conserved quantity. The quadrature follows directly from the stated Hamiltonian.
fate: This is the classical one-degree-of-freedom example; \citet[Section~4.5]{cannas2007introduction} treats the equivalent shifted pendulum Hamiltonian and its critical levels.

title: The periodic Toda Hamiltonian
notes: The first Toda potential is written as a difference of exponentials, with a summation index \(k\) but exponents using \(n\). P000619 instead gives \(U=g^2\sum_{k=1}^n e^{-(q_{k+1}-q_k)}\); P000618 states \(q_{k+n}=q_k\).
statement:
For \(n\geq3\), take the phase space \(T^*\mathbb R^n\), canonical brackets, and the periodic convention \(q_{n+1}=q_1\). The corrected Hamiltonian is
     \[H=\tfrac12\sum_{k=1}^np_k^2+g^2\sum_{k=1}^ne^{q_k-q_{k+1}}.\]
     The difference of neighboring exponentials belongs in the force equation \(\dot p_k=g^2(e^{q_{k-1}-q_k}-e^{q_k-q_{k+1}})\). Summing such differences as the potential would telescope to zero after correcting the index.
reconstruction: The potential is restored from the explicit repetition on P000619. The open chain has a different boundary convention and is not silently substituted for the periodic system.

title: Involution of the Toda integrals

title: Five pair-potential families and their phase spaces
notes: The table lists \(q^{-2}\), \(a^2\sinh^{-2}(aq)\), \(a^2\sin^{-2}(aq)\), \(a^2\wp(aq)\), and \(q^{-2}+a^2q^2\), first for \(U=g^2\sum_{i<j}V(q_i-q_j)\). The hyperbolic and trigonometric cases are called limits of the elliptic case.
statement:
For \(n\) particles on the line, use canonical coordinates \((q_i,p_i)\) on the cotangent bundle of a collision-free configuration chamber; exclude all poles of \(V\). The trigonometric model may instead be interpreted on a circle, with collisions modulo its period excluded. In the elliptic model choose periods and a real slice on which the potential is real. The fifth pair potential leaves the center of mass free:
     \(\sum_{i<j}(q_i-q_j)^2=n\sum_i(q_i-Q_{\rm cm})^2\).
     Thus its relative motion has harmonic confinement, while a one-body trap \(\frac12\omega^2\sum q_i^2\) also confines the center of mass. Elliptic degenerations give the first three potentials up to scale and additive constants.
reconstruction: The domains, reality conditions and separation of center-of-mass motion are supplied. No integrability claim is inferred for arbitrary singular continuations or boundary identifications.

title: Classical and nonreduced root-system potentials
notes: The second family adds \(V(q_i+q_j)\), \(V(q_i)\), and \(V(2q_i)\). P000619 rewrites this as \(\sum_{\alpha>0}g_\alpha^2V((\alpha,q))\), with equal couplings for equal root lengths, and identifies types \(A,B,C,BC,D\).
statement:
Let \(R\) be a finite crystallographic root system, or the standard nonreduced \(BC_r\), in a Euclidean space \(\mathfrak a\). On \(T^*\mathfrak a_{\rm reg}\), away from the potential's root hyperplanes or affine pole walls, set
     \[H=\tfrac12(p,p)+\sum_{\alpha\in R_+}c_\alpha V((\alpha,q)),\]
     with couplings constant on Weyl orbits. The roots \(e_i-e_j\) yield \(A_{n-1}\) for \(n\) particles after separating the center of mass; \(e_i\pm e_j,e_i,2e_i\) yield the \(BC\) family. In the displayed \(B\) formula the plus and minus pair terms must have compatible Weyl-invariant coefficients; an arbitrary independent \(\varepsilon\) is not covered by this statement.
reconstruction: The shift from \(A_n\) to \(A_{n-1}\) records the usual rank convention. Weyl-orbit coupling and regular-domain hypotheses are made explicit. This item is the construction, distinct from the exceptional-case integrability question.
fate: The speaker's joint work gives this root-system framework in \citet[Section~2]{olshanetskyperelomov1978radial}; that 1978 paper itself cites the classical 1976 construction. The match is to the stated family, not to every arbitrary coefficient suggested by the shorthand.

title: Commuting complete integrals in the elliptic case
notes: In row 4, conserved quantities for the elliptic potential are credited to Calogero and Olshanetsky--Perelomov, while the involution column contains two question marks, corresponding to families A and B.
statement: For the unreduced \(n\)-particle elliptic Calogero--Moser system on \(T^*Q_{\rm reg}\), where \(Q_{\rm reg}\subset\mathbb R^n\) (or \(\mathbb C^n\)) excludes every pair difference at a potential pole, do there exist \(n\) generically independent meromorphic integrals in involution, including the free center-of-mass momentum? After removing the center-of-mass canonical pair, the relative \(A_{n-1}\) problem instead needs \(n-1\) integrals. The analogous root-system question requires orbit-constant couplings. The assertion concerns generic regular points, not a uniform action--angle chart through collisions or singular fibers.

title: Four separate tasks in solving an integrable model
notes: Gelfand lists: find the integrals, prove involution, solve the inverse problem, and express the solution by quadratures.
statement: Conservation, \(\{I_j,H\}=0\), does not imply mutual involution or functional independence. Liouville integration requires a complete independent commuting family on a regular region. An inverse problem additionally requires specification of spectral data and its equivalences; quadrature or explicit inversion is a further constructive step. Consequently the table's question marks concern different mathematical assertions.

title: Lax matrices and trace invariants
notes: For types 1--4, \(I_k=\operatorname{Sp}(L^k)\), with \(L=P+iX\), \(P_{ij}=p_i\delta_{ij}\), and \(X_{ij}=(1-\delta_{ij})x(q_i-q_j)\). The table gives \(x=q^{-1},a\coth(aq),a\cot(aq),a\,\operatorname{cn}(aq)/\operatorname{sn}(aq)\).
statement:
An exact rational reconstruction is
     \[L_{ij}=p_i\delta_{ij}+\frac{ig(1-\delta_{ij})}{q_i-q_j},\qquad
     M_{ij}=-\frac{ig}{(q_i-q_j)^2}\ (i\ne j),\quad M_{ii}=ig\sum_{j\ne i}(q_i-q_j)^{-2}.\]
     For \(H=\frac12\sum p_i^2+g^2\sum_{i<j}(q_i-q_j)^{-2}\), Hamilton's equations give \(\dot L=[L,M]\), hence every \(\operatorname{tr}L^k\) is conserved and \(H=\frac12\operatorname{tr}L^2\). This argument alone does not prove involution. The nonrational kernels require compatible diagonal terms, coupling and elliptic-period conventions; the table alone does not specify these.

title: The quadratic matrix invariant for harmonic confinement
notes: For type 5 the notes use \(N=L^2+\omega^2Q^2\), \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(q_i)\), and \(I_k=\operatorname{Sp}(N^k)\).
statement:
For the rational Calogero Hamiltonian with a one-body harmonic trap, the rational matrices satisfy
     \(\dot L=[L,M]-\omega^2Q\), \(\dot Q=[Q,M]+L\).
     Therefore \(N=L^2+\omega^2Q^2\) satisfies \(\dot N=[N,M]\), and \(\operatorname{tr}N^k\) is conserved. For the pairwise quadratic potential on P000618 this applies to the relative variables after separating the free center of mass and matching the frequency; with the table's coefficients, \(\omega^2=2ng^2a^2\). Conservation of these traces is the assertion verified here, not a separate proof that this particular list is independent and in involution.

title: Inverse spectral data require more than the traces

statement: The traces determine the characteristic polynomial of a finite matrix, not its entries or the full phase point. Even in the rational family, \(q_i\mapsto q_i+c\) leaves \(L\) unchanged. title: Quantum Hamiltonians as conjugated radial Laplacians

statement: For a Riemannian symmetric space, restriction of the Laplace--Beltrami operator to invariant functions gives a radial differential operator with first-derivative terms. Conjugation by the square root of the radial density removes them and produces a Schrödinger operator of Calogero--Sutherland type, up to an additive constant and scale. The couplings are determined by the restricted-root multiplicities. The compact, noncompact and flat cases lead respectively to trigonometric, hyperbolic and rational interactions. title: Classical Grassmann coordinates and the graded Poisson bracket
notes: Fradkin allows Bose and Fermi canonical variables, writes \(pq+qp=1\) after Grassmann variables, and then introduces a Poisson bracket using right and left derivatives and the parities \(n_A,n_B\).
statement:
Classical odd coordinates in a supercommutative algebra satisfy \(\theta_a\theta_b=-\theta_b\theta_a\), so their algebra product does not obey \(pq+qp=1\). That relation belongs to quantized creation and annihilation operators, or to an odd multiplication operator paired with differentiation. An even graded Poisson bracket instead satisfies
     \[\{A,B\}=-(-1)^{|A||B|}\{B,A\},\qquad
       \{A,BC\}=\{A,B\}C+(-1)^{|A||B|}B\{A,C\}.\]
     Canonical even pairs obey \(\{q_i,p_j\}=\delta_{ij}\), while an odd canonical pair has a symmetric bracket \(\{\theta_a,\pi_b\}=\{\pi_b,\theta_a\}=\delta_{ab}\), after choosing left/right derivative conventions.
reconstruction: The algebra product, the classical graded bracket and the quantum anticommutator are separated. This removes the contradiction while preserving the intended mixed canonical formalism.
fate: The basic distinction is algebraic and predates the talk; Berezin is explicitly named in the record. The later general constrained formalism in \citet[abstract, publication lead]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization} matches the theme, but its inaccessible full text is not used to certify the notebook's derivative signs.

title: Gauge constraints and the two photon polarizations
notes: Electromagnetism and Yang--Mills theory are examples of constrained systems; light has two states rather than three because gauge invariance removes an extra state.
statement: For free Maxwell theory in \(3+1\)-dimensional Minkowski space, a nonzero null momentum has a transverse polarization space modulo gauge shifts \(\epsilon_\mu\mapsto\epsilon_\mu+\lambda k_\mu\). This quotient is two-dimensional, corresponding to two physical helicities. In Hamiltonian language the primary and Gauss constraints, together with gauge equivalence, remove the unphysical canonical variables. The assertion does not count polarizations of a massive vector field, which has a different constraint structure.
reconstruction: The spacetime dimension, massless free field and gauge quotient are supplied to make the numerical assertion definite.
fate: The constraint and polarization analysis is checked in \citet[Sections~6.1--6.2]{tong2006qft}; this is established Maxwell theory, used as an example rather than a new 1975 result.

title: The singular Legendre map and the constraint algorithm
notes: The momentum is defined by a right derivative of \(L\); failure to solve for \(\dot q\), expressed by a vanishing Hessian determinant, leads to additional constraints and the Dirac procedure.
statement: For an ordinary finite-dimensional Lagrangian \(L(q,\dot q)\), an invertible velocity Hessian gives a local Legendre transformation by the inverse function theorem. A constant-rank singular Legendre map has a locally constrained image. Preservation of primary constraints under Hamiltonian evolution can impose secondary constraints, fix multipliers, or reveal gauge freedom. In a Bose--Fermi system the relevant invertibility is that of a graded linear map; an ordinary determinant is inadequate for a general mixed Hessian.
reconstruction: Constant-rank and local regularity assumptions are supplied. Singular rank-changing Lagrangians are not covered by a statement that all constraints automatically form a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with constant structure coefficients.
fate: The regular Legendre step is recalled in \citet[Appendix~C.4]{cannas2007introduction}. The mixed constrained extension is the subject of the later Fradkin--Fradkina publication lead, whose exact formula has not been read \citep{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}.

title: First- and second-class constraints require a rank condition
notes: Second-class constraints are described by brackets \(\{\varphi_k,\psi_j\}\ne0\) after imposing the other constraints, with central constraints discarded.
statement:
On a regular constraint surface, a first-class function has bracket zero on that surface with every constraint. A selected family \(\chi_a\) is second class when its bracket matrix \(C_{ab}=\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}\) is invertible on the surface (in the graded sense when needed). A nonzero matrix entry alone is insufficient. For purely even second-class constraints,
     \[\{F,G\}_D=\{F,G\}-\{F,\chi_a\}(C^{-1})^{ab}\{\chi_b,G\}\]
     is the Dirac bracket, under the usual regularity assumptions. First-class constraints may close with phase-space-dependent structure functions rather than constants.
reconstruction: The invertibility condition replaces the notebook's entrywise nonvanishing shorthand. The displayed bracket is explicitly restricted to the ungraded case so that no missing super-sign convention is hidden.
fate: This is the Dirac distinction named in the note. The relation with general Bose--Fermi quantization is only indirectly identified through \citet[abstract, publication lead]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}; the original Dirac book edition is not specified here.

title: Sources and the formal generating functional
notes: The displayed \(Z\) integrates fields and canonical momenta against constraint delta functions and an exponential of the Hamiltonian action plus sources. It is called the generating function of all Green functions and an analogue of a Fourier transform.
statement: Formally, with fixed boundary or vacuum prescription and consistent factors of \(i\), one writes \(Z[J]=C^{-1}\int D\mu\,e^{iS+i\langle J,\Phi\rangle}\). Functional derivatives with respect to even and odd sources generate the corresponding ordered correlation functions. The measure \(D\mu\), constraint reduction or gauge fixing, regularization, and source parity must be specified. This symbolic integral is not a countably additive Lebesgue measure on an infinite-dimensional field space, and the line alone does not define all quantum theories.
reconstruction: Only the formal generating-functional mechanism is reconstructed. The notebook's crossed-out measure and uncertain grouping are not silently converted into a rigorous path-integral theorem.
fate: Formal source differentiation gives the generating mechanism; the Wick expansion read in \citet[Section~3.3]{tong2006qft} checks the corresponding perturbative correlation-function structure, not existence of the displayed measure. A more specific subsequent constrained construction is suggested by \citet[abstract, publication lead]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}, but an exact formula-by-formula identification has not been verified.

title: The constraint determinant and the ambiguous term A
notes: The term \(A\) contains trace logarithms of even and odd constraint brackets and a Schur-complement expression. It appears after the exponent's integral, while another exponential and \(\delta(0)/2\) occur inside the definition of \(A\).
statement:
A finite-dimensional model for regular second-class reduction inserts the constraint delta function and the square root of the determinant of the bracket matrix; with even and odd constraints the corresponding object is a square root of a Berezinian, with conventions fixed. For a block matrix \(C=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&B\\ C_1&D\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) with invertible odd block \(D\),
     \[\operatorname{Ber}C=\frac{\det(A-BD^{-1}C_1)}{\det D}.\]
     This explains the visible Schur complement and difference of trace logarithms. It does not determine the notebook's misplaced exponential, numerical coefficient, sign, or distributional factor. First-class systems also require gauge fixing or its equivalent.
reconstruction: The Berezinian is an explicit algebraic reconstruction of the visible pattern; the complete \(A\) formula remains unresolved. No universal determinant formula for arbitrary quantum field theories is claimed.
fate: The abstract of the 1978 Fradkin--Fradkina lead concerns precisely mixed first- and second-class constraints, but its full text was inaccessible \citep{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}. The exact displayed expression therefore remains a partial, indirect identification rather than a verified publication match.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The regular determinant/Berezinian mechanism is standard; the exact notebook term A has not been recovered.

title: Differential parts of fractional powers and the KdV hierarchy
notes: For \(L=-D^2+u\), \(A=D^3+\cdots\) is described as \(L^{3/2}\) with nondifferential terms cut off. The same operation on \(L^{5/2},L^{7/2},\ldots\) leaves a commutator that is multiplication by a function.
statement:
Use the formal pseudodifferential algebra and choose \(R=(-L)^{1/2}=D+O(D^{-1})\). Then \(B_{2j+1}=(R^{2j+1})_+\), the part with nonnegative powers of \(D\), satisfies \([B_{2j+1},L]\) of differential order at most zero. For \(j=1\),
     \[B_3=D^3-\tfrac32uD-\tfrac34u',\qquad [L,B_3]=\tfrac32uu'-\tfrac14u'''.\]
     Thus the corresponding Lax equation gives KdV after a constant time rescaling. The formal higher flows commute; analytic existence for particular function spaces is a separate issue.
reconstruction: The branch and sign are essential: \(L=-D^2+u\) has no formal square root with leading term \(D\). The construction is algebraic, not the spectral fractional power of an unbounded self-adjoint operator.
fate: The hierarchy was already discussed in 1973-326.1 and 1973-327.1, so the present statement is expository. A systematic later fractional-operator treatment is read in \citet[Sections~8--12]{gelfanddikii1976fractional}, received 22 June 1976 and published that year.

title: The stationary third-order equation and one-gap potentials
notes: A one-zone potential is identified by \(K(u)=0\), so that the second- and third-order operators commute; this is called a hypothesis in the notes.
statement:
For a real smooth periodic potential, the existence of a normalized third-order commuting operator gives a stationary KdV equation
     \[u'''-6uu'+cu'=0\]
     for a constant \(c\). For example \(A=-4D^3+6uD+3u'-cD\) obeys \([A,-D^2+u]=6uu'-u'''-cu'\). Such periodic stationary solutions have at most one finite open spectral gap; the nonconstant nonsingular elliptic case has one, and constant or degenerate cases must be distinguished. A general one-gap potential need not obey the unshifted equation with \(c=0\).
reconstruction: Real smooth periodicity, the lower-flow constant, and the meaning of one finite open gap are supplied. The algebraic commutator calculation by itself does not establish a band-spectrum statement for arbitrary complex or nonperiodic coefficients.
fate: \citet[Section~2, Theorem~2.1 and the \(n=1\) example on p.~63]{novikov1974periodic} verifies the stationary-to-finite-gap implication before this talk. The converse characterization belongs to the earlier problem GP-1974-10, represented here by its one-gap occurrence; see also 1974-340.7 and 1974-343.2.

title: Coefficient recursion for a commuting operator
notes: Expanding \([L_n,L_m]=0\) gives coefficient equations. The first \(m-1\) equations express the \(v_i\) as differential polynomials in the \(u_i\), with integration constants; the first relation is \(v_{m-2}=(m/n)u_{n-2}+h_2\).
statement:
Work locally with scalar differential operators over a characteristic-zero differential field, with constant nonzero leading coefficients. After scaling, let
     \(L_n=D^n+\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}u_jD^j\), while \(L_m=D^m+cD^{m-1}+\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}v_jD^j\), with \(n,m\geq2\) and \(c\) constant. Equating the coefficient of \(D^{n+m-3}\) gives
     \(nv'_{m-2}-mu'_{n-2}=0\), hence the displayed relation. Recursive comparison determines the lower \(v_j\) as differential polynomials with constants; the remaining \(n-1\) equations constrain the \(u_j\). For \(n=2\) and odd \(m\), these are stationary higher-KdV equations.
reconstruction: The monic normalization and vanishing \(D^{n-1}\) coefficient are supplied. One common scalar gauge can remove that coefficient of \(L_n\); it need not simultaneously remove the constant \(D^{m-1}\) coefficient of an arbitrary commuting partner.
fate: This elimination is part of the systematic formal-operator framework in \citet[Sections~8--12]{gelfanddikii1976fractional}; Krichever's normalization is explicit in \citet[Section~2.1]{krichever1977methods}. The subsequent algebraic-geometric solution is more than this coefficient count.
